How would you deal with a rose garden which has blackspot everywhere? It is a year on year problem.

What has been tried:

  • Plucking infected leaves and disposing of them
  • Spraying once a fortnight
  • The rose stock is meant to be good. The roses do bloom.

Daconil is an effective and relatively safe fungicide. I use it on my tomatoes early in the season if the weather is overly damp. I avoid Bayer Rose products because many of them have systemic insecticides that are deadly to bees. In addition to pollinators, I have leaf cutter bees on my roses every year which I don't want to harm.

Some people rotate fungicides...using a different one each time they spray. Some fungicides are pretty nasty though so I limit myself to the one. I tend to steer clear of finicky rose types though so I don't have major problems with them.

With any chemical you use, read and follow the label carefully.

The secret success for most fungicides is understanding that they are a preventative, not a cure. You're doing the right things...it may just be timing or technique. Removing infected leaves is essential. Additionally, you really have to cover a plant as completely as possible (without excessive run-off) with Daconil as it actually forms a physical barrier to prevent fungus from attacking plant tissues.

Another thing you might want to check for is rose borers. When you prune, the open stem ends will allow borers to enter the cane. You'll see a hole, browning, and bulges if you have them. They are easy to prevent by dabbing a bit of Elmer's glue on the wound right after you cut it. Mine were infested for years without me knowing it and once I started adding the glue, my plants got much healthier.
